Seats where the winner had no opponent after the primary are marked. Question wording needs a final check. Your ballot is the final word.
statewideNote: Every Hawaii voter decides these 2 Proposed Constitutional Amendments.

statewide.title: More time for the state Senate to confirm judges
statewide.what: Shall the Constitution of the State of Hawaii be amended to allow the Senate more time to consider and act on the appointments of justices and judges, by increasing the timeframe from thirty days to sixty days for appointments made between April 1 and December 31 when the senate is not in regular session or is about to adjourn the regular session?
statewide.yes: The Senate gets 60 days instead of 30 to act on judges picked between April 1 and December 31.
statewide.no: The Senate keeps 30 days to act on every judge pick, all year.
statewide.needs: more yes votes than no votes, and yes votes equal to at least half of all ballots cast

statewide.title: RISE bonds: counties borrow for housing infrastructure, repaid from new property tax growth
statewide.what: Shall the Hawaii State Constitution be amended to direct the legislature to authorize the counties to issue resilient infrastructure for shelter and equity bonds to fund public improvements in designated districts, repaid solely by future growth in property tax revenues within those districts, not by increasing real property tax rates, where such bonds are excluded from the counties’ debt limit and are subject to accountability and oversight requirements as may be provided by law?
statewide.yes: Counties could, once the Legislature sets rules, borrow for housing infrastructure and repay it only from new property tax growth in a set district, outside their debt limit.
statewide.no: Counties could not issue RISE bonds; infrastructure would still be paid for with existing kinds of borrowing under the debt limit.
statewide.needs: more yes votes than no votes, and yes votes equal to at least half of all ballots cast
